explainer.title: How to read this screen
explainer.p1: Tessera is confronted with a catalogue of publicly documented agent failures — prompt injection, PII leaks, hallucination, overconfidence. Every run replays the same cases against a model and counts what breaks.
explainer.p2: The floor is measured with no model at all: a large share of the cases is already held by the deterministic guards (firewall, refusals). An absolute score is therefore not the grade — what matters is what the model adds above the floor, and what it breaks that the guard held on its own.
explainer.p3: BLOCKED · rule 1 means a certified break — reproduced across repeated passes — forbids the release regardless of the average score: one observation is enough to see a break, never to prove its absence.

compare.locked: A run is a case set × ONE model. “Compare two models on a run” does not exist: the référentiel is chosen first, then two models among the runs that were scored against it.
compare.offReferential: ⚠ These two runs did NOT run on the same case set ({a} vs {b}). The gap between them is a gap of TEST before it is a gap of model — it is not attributable to the model alone.
compare.costWhy: Comparing quality without cost is half a decision.
compare.sizeBuysNothing: A counter-intuitive result, measured on this sweep: {bigger} ({biggerB} billion parameters) contributes LESS than {smaller} ({smallerB} billion). On this catalogue, model size buys nothing. That is a result, not an anecdote.
compare.disagreements: {count, plural, =0 {No disagreement} one {# disagreement} other {# disagreements}}
compare.disagreementsWhy: The cases where both models say the same thing discriminate nothing: they are left out ({agreed} runs). A break of the floor sorts first — nothing outranks being worse than having no model.
compare.byCategory: Delta by category — a model is not better on average, it is better somewhere

bench.title: The bench's own honesty

silence.title: Cases an EMPTY response would pass
silence.body: {weak} of the {total} cases are passed by a system that does nothing: their criteria are purely negative (“must not contain”). The guard refuses, the IBAN is not in the refusal, ✅. That is why the floor reaches 70% — and it means that on these cases, silence is indistinguishable from competence.

zeroPower.title: Categories that can grade no model at all
zeroPower.body: {categories}: the guard passes them IN FULL, with no model. Their discriminating power over a model is zero — derived from the committed baseline, never listed by hand.
zeroPower.none: No category is held entirely by the guard: all of them can, in principle, grade a model.

coverage.title: Declared-capability coverage: inexpressible
coverage.inexpressible: The coverage map (cases × the agents' declared capabilities) cannot be drawn, and not for want of trying: the case schema (`eval/failures/_schema.json`, `additionalProperties: false`) declares NO field through which a case could name a capability. So the coverage is not empty — it is inexpressible. A map drawn over a join that does not exist would read as complete while being invented. The fix is a GOVERNED change to the case set; this screen reveals the hole, it cannot fill it.
coverage.expressible: The case schema now declares a capability field: the coverage map can be drawn on a real key. It remains to be built.
coverage.schemaUnreadable: The case schema could not be read. The coverage is not asserted absent — it is undetermined, which is not the same claim.

matrix.title: Case × language matrix
matrix.subtitle: A run is not a flat pass/fail. A model can pass in French and fail in German — and a green cell can be green with NO model at all.
matrix.noFloor: No committed floor: what the guard holds on its own cannot be told apart from what the model contributes. The cells stay undetermined rather than falsely attributed.

fixes.prompt_injection: Harden the guard's input filtering and the system-instruction reminder; never expose the system prompt.
fixes.pii_leak: Harden the PII/tools layer: mask PAN/IBAN and refuse access to third-party data before any tool call.
fixes.hallucination: Require a retrieved citation (RAG) before any factual claim; with no source, answer with uncertainty.
fixes.overconfidence: Recalibrate and lower the confidence thresholds, and force a hedge or retraction above the threshold.
fixes.citation_fabrication: Allow only citations backed by a retrieved passage; block any reference absent from the corpus.
fixes.tool_misuse: Require an authorization check and human escalation before any destructive or sensitive action.
fixes.policy_violation: Tighten the guard rules (policy.yaml) and explicitly refuse anti-fraud evasion attempts.
fixes.regulatory_misstatement: Ground regulatory answers (DORA/GDPR/BaFin/CNIL) in the cited corpus; strengthen RAG grounding rather than the raw model.
fixes.language_mixing: Pin the response language to the request's (prompt + post-check) to avoid language drift.
fixes.escalation_failure: Wire human escalation for out-of-scope or unauthenticated cases instead of answering directly.
fixes.unknown: Uncategorized case: analyze the failure reason manually, then map it to a catalogue category.

power.title: What the catalogue measures
power.notMeasured: The catalogue's discriminating power has not been measured. It is measured (make eval-power-write), never declared.
power.unreadable: The measurement EXISTS and this code cannot read it — that is not an absence, it is a blind spot: {reason}. Reporting "not measured yet" would present our ignorance as a property of the world.
power.offReferential: Classification VOID: it was measured on référentiel {measured}, and the catalogue is now {current}. Its counts describe cases that no longer exist — re-measure, do not reinterpret.

bucket.factDetail: {dead} dead (silence closes them) · {inverted} inverted (the model is worse than silence) · {saturated} saturated · {unreached} unreached. No p-value, no power: one does not test a fact.
bucket.certifiedDetail: {discriminating} discriminating · {reversed} reversed (the WEAK model wins). The inference survived the multiplicity correction.
bucket.cannotSayDetail: A real difference below {mde} points, which this many passes cannot certify. These cases are NOT dead: they are unknown, and the remedy is more passes, not a firmer adjective.
bucket.cannotSayNoPower: This design could have certified nothing, whatever it observed. Not one of these cases may be called dead or non-discriminating.

power.mde: This design ({strongN} + {weakN} passes) is blind to anything under a {mde}-point separation. Any smaller effect is "cannot say" — never "no effect".
power.corrections: Holm certifies {holm} runs (it feeds the ratchet — it must never count a discriminator that isn't one); Benjamini-Hochberg certifies {bh} (it feeds the diagnosis). The gap between them: {gap}.
power.headline: {measured, plural, =0 {Not one case of # actually measures the model.} one {# case of {total} actually measures the model.} other {# cases of {total} actually measure the model.}}
power.method: Derived from the null control and {strongN} + {weakN} full passes. A case discriminates if it separates the two models (Fisher exact, one-tailed, corrected across the whole catalogue); inverted if the null control passes it and the model that ships reproducibly breaks it — the agent is worse than silence there.
power.warning: The null control — no model, zero tokens — already passes 122 of the 174 runs. A dead case tests the deterministic layer (guard, router), not the model: it inflates the pass rate and measures nothing about the model.

etat.what: Quality state right now: global score, controls failing or on alert, current release impact, and the period-over-period evolution.
etat.how: Aggregates the faithfulness SLO, the count of off-target signals, and the latest release diff.

diagnostic.what: Why quality drifts: failures by type, judge calibration, priority cases, and root cause.
diagnostic.how: Documented failure catalogue + clustering of failed cases + version diff.

predictive.what: Early-warning signals of a regression: regression risk, judge drift, failure predictor, intent, and localization.
predictive.how: Risk models over the score series and metric drift.

actions.what: Concrete actions to take, derived from open regressions and real failed cases.
actions.how: One recommendation is generated per open regression or case cluster.

scoreGlobal.what: The global quality score out of 100: share of answers judged compliant (faithfulness SLO).
scoreGlobal.how: Compliant answers ÷ evaluated answers, scaled to 100.

nonRegression.what: Non-regression rate: share of cases that did not degrade versus the baseline version.

regressionsOpen.what: The number of regressions still open versus the baseline.
regressionsOpen.how: Cases whose score dropped beyond noise and not yet resolved.

judgeKappa.what: Agreement (Cohen's kappa) between the LLM judge and the human reference annotations.
judgeKappa.how: Kappa over a gold set; above 0.6 = substantial agreement.

casEval.what: The number of catalogue cases evaluated in the latest non-regression run.
casEval.how: Cases executed by the evaluation harness.

faithfulness.what: Faithfulness: the answer stays true to the cited sources, without extrapolation.
faithfulness.how: Mean judge score on faithfulness; the delta compares to the start of the period.

grounding.what: Grounding: the answer rests on passages that were actually retrieved.
grounding.how: Mean grounding score; delta over the period.

hallucination.what: Hallucination: claims not supported by the sources.
hallucination.how: Mean score on the metric; a higher score is better (measured absence of hallucination).

faithGrounding.what: The faithfulness × grounding scatter: each point is a turn; top-right = both faithful and grounded.
faithGrounding.how: Per-turn (faithfulness, grounding) pairs; colour summarises the mean of the two.

failureDistribution.what: The distribution of failed cases by failure type (injection, PII leak, hallucination…).
failureDistribution.how: Count of failed cases grouped by category, top 5.

judgeCalibration.what: How reliable the LLM judge is: agreement with humans, verbosity bias, and sample size.
judgeCalibration.how: Kappa + agreement over a gold set; correlation to answer length.

priorityCases.what: The most severe failed cases to handle first, sorted by severity.

sigActive.what: Number of quality signals instrumented and evaluated live, out of the 200 in the reference catalogue.
sigActive.how: One row per signal derived from the live reports (SLO, calibration, citations, guardrails, PII, cost, routing…); « / 200 » places coverage within the catalogue. The curve and delta come from the durable status journal.

sigCrit.what: Signals whose live value breaches the critical threshold (red band).
sigCrit.how: Status = measured value against the signal threshold; « critical » when the critical threshold is breached. Delta and curve from the durable status journal.

sigWarn.what: Signals in the warning band: degraded but below the critical threshold.
sigWarn.how: Measured value between the warning and critical thresholds.

sigOk.what: Signals that meet their quality threshold.
sigOk.how: Measured value at or above the expected level.

sigNa.what: Signals with no live measurement yet — shown « — » rather than a fabricated value.
sigNa.how: No report available for the period; Tessera's no-mock discipline.

sigRegistry.what: Full signal catalogue, grouped by severity, with each signal's value, threshold and status.
sigRegistry.how: One row per metric (code shown, e.g. rag.faithfulness.mean); status derived from value vs threshold; filterable by entity and status.

sigTheme.what: Distribution of signals by family: fidelity, security, compliance, reliability, sessions.
sigTheme.how: Count of signals per category, as a share of the total.
sigTheme.source: Category carried by each catalogue signal.

sigHeatmap.what: Concentration of signals by owning entity (answer, judge, corpus, guardrail…) and severity.
sigHeatmap.how: Count of signals for each (entity, status) pair; intensity follows the count.

sigRailFiche.what: Detail of the selected signal: metric code, value, threshold, source and scope.
sigRailFiche.how: Fields of the row selected in the registry.

sigRailCases.what: Documented failure cases attached to the quality signals.
sigRailCases.how: Excerpts from the non-regression failure catalogue.

sigRailRelease.what: Production version and the state of the quality gates (deploy blocked when regressions are open).
sigRailRelease.how: Blocked when the number of open regressions is greater than 0.

sigRailActivity.what: Latest quality events: last run, release, configuration change.
sigRailActivity.how: Aggregate of the last eval run, the current release and the configuration diff.

sigRailActions.what: Governed remediations proposed from the current state of the gates and regressions.
sigRailActions.how: Derived from release status and open cases; some require dual control.

evolution.what: Mean fidelity score day by day over the current window.
evolution.how: Per-bucket mean from the score journal; gaps with no eval stay empty (never a fabricated zero); the delta compares to the first bucket.

runRuns.what: Number of evaluation runs executed in the current window, relative to the registry total.
runRuns.how: Count of runs in the window; « / N » = archived total.

runCatalogue.what: Version of the failure catalogue evaluated and the languages covered.
runCatalogue.how: Version and languages declared by the run registry.

runCases.what: Total cases replayed over the window, relative to the catalogue size.
runCases.how: Sum of cases per run; « / N » = catalogue cases.

runDrift.what: Mean absolute run-over-run drift across the themed datasets.
runDrift.how: Mean of |drift| per dataset; « n/a » when no data.

runCost.what: Cumulative evaluation cost over the window (euros).
runCost.how: Sum of estimated costs of priced runs; « free » when local.

runRelease.what: Production version; tinted by open regressions.
runRelease.how: Current version; warns when regressions are open.

runDuration.what: Mean run latency over the window; subtitle = stale corpora.
runDuration.how: Mean of per-run latencies; stale corpora from the freshness report.

runTable.what: Log of archived evaluation runs: model, cases, pass-rate, delta, cost.
runTable.how: One row per run; delta = pass-rate vs the same model's previous run.

runCtx.what: Metadata of the selected run: model, dataset, timestamp, cost, latency.
runCtx.how: Fields of the run picked in the table.

runDatasets.what: Themed datasets evaluated, with cases, coverage and drift.
runDatasets.how: One row per theme of the failure catalogue.

runChPassrate.what: Pass-rate of the latest full runs, oldest to newest.
runChPassrate.how: Runs with 10 or more cases, sorted by date, last 12.

runChCoverage.what: Share of the dataset covered by evaluation, per theme.

runChDrift.what: Mean run-over-run drift per theme, largest magnitude first.

runChDistribution.what: Distribution of evaluation cases by theme; centre = total cases.
runChDistribution.how: Cases per dataset; total in the donut centre.

runChCostQuality.what: Cost per model set against pass-rate, models sorted by success.
runChCostQuality.how: Estimated cost and pass-rate per model; zero cost skipped.

runRailRelease.how: Current version; warning badge when regressions remain open.

runRailDatasets.what: Number of monitored datasets and coverage share.

runRailActivity.what: Latest archived runs, newest to oldest.
runRailActivity.how: The four most recent runs in the archive.

runRailHealth.what: Pipeline operations signals: jobs, workers, queue, freshness.
runRailHealth.how: Jobs in window and freshness are real; workers/queue « — » with no source (never a fake OK).

failTotal.what: Total number of failed evaluation cases over the window.
failTotal.how: Count of failed cases in the archive; the curve follows the trend.

failCritical.what: Failed cases of critical severity; subtitle = share of total.
failCritical.how: Cases flagged « critical »; percent of total.

failNew.what: Failed cases seen for the first time.
failNew.how: Cases never recorded before; percent of total.

failRecurrent.what: Failed cases that recur from one run to the next.
failRecurrent.how: Cases already seen in previous runs; percent of total.

failDistribution.what: Distribution of failed cases by failure category.
failDistribution.how: Count per category; donut centre = total.

failEvolution.what: Evolution of the failed-case count over time.
failEvolution.how: Cases per time bucket, stacked by severity.

failCauses.what: Top five root causes by case count.

failSla.what: Triage markers: mean latency, critical/new share, models affected.
failSla.how: Mean case latency, shares, distinct model count.

failFiche.what: Full detail of the selected failed case: prompt, response, expected, reasons.
failFiche.how: Fields of the case picked in the list.

modelReferent.what: Reference model of the comparison (best first).
modelReferent.how: First model in the pass-rate ranking.

modelScore.what: Success score of the reference model, out of 100, with the gap to the previous reading.
modelScore.how: pass_rate × 100; delta = last bucket vs previous.

modelFaith.what: Mean faithfulness of the reference model.

modelGrounding.what: Grounding rate of the reference model.
modelGrounding.how: Share of answers grounded in sources.

modelNonReg.how: Share of cases with no regression at the last gate.

modelHallucination.what: Anti-hallucination safety of the reference (1 minus the hallucination rate).
modelHallucination.how: 100 minus the reference hallucination rate, in %.

modelKappa.how: Kappa of the LLM judge against the annotated standard.

modelCases.what: Cases evaluated for the reference; subtitle = active models.
modelCases.how: Reference case count; N models compared.

modelScoreByModel.what: Pass-rate per model over time, over the selected period.
modelScoreByModel.how: Per-model series from the run archive, bounded to the period.

modelRadar.what: Per-metric profile of each model (faithfulness, grounding…).

modelHeatmap.what: Pass-rate per model and case category.

modelFaithGrounding.what: Faithfulness vs grounding scatter per model.
modelFaithGrounding.how: One point per model: faithfulness on x, grounding on y.

modelCostQuality.what: Cost vs pass-rate scatter per model.
modelCostQuality.how: One point per model: estimated cost on x, pass-rate on y.

modelRecentRuns.what: Pass-rate of recent runs over the selected period.
modelRecentRuns.how: Recent runs bounded to the period, by date.

modelTable.what: Detailed per-model table: score, faithfulness, grounding, cost, cases.

modelIntent.what: Performance by intent — unavailable: Tessera has no model × intent labels.
modelIntent.how: No real source; the panel shows « unavailable » rather than a fabricated value.

modelDrift.what: Judge drift (faithfulness, grounding), consensus and series stability.
modelDrift.how: Judge drift, inter-judge consensus and score-series variance.

modelPeriod.what: Narrows score-over-time and recent runs to a window of real run dates.
modelPeriod.how: Selection of N days anchored on an existing run date.

jgKappa.what: Cohen's kappa between the LLM judge and the human label on the gold set.

jgAgreement.what: Raw agreement rate between judge and human on the gold set.
jgAgreement.how: Share of points where judge and human agree.

jgFp.what: False positives: the judge says « good », the human says « no ».
jgFp.how: FP relative to the number of gold points.

jgFn.what: False negatives: the judge says « no », the human says « good ».
jgFn.how: FN relative to the number of gold points.

jgVerbosity.what: Verbosity bias: correlation between answer length and judge score.

jgClemency.what: Leniency: mean score the judge gives to cases the human rated bad.
jgClemency.how: Mean score on « bad » cases; lower is better.

jgDrift.what: Judge drift over time versus the baseline.
jgDrift.how: Divergence of the judge's readings; warns beyond 0.10.

jgDisagree.what: Number of gold cases where judge and human diverge; hint = human overrides.
jgDisagree.how: Count of points with no agreement; overrides = human corrections.

jgConfusion.what: 2×2 judge × human matrix (TP/FP/FN/TN) on the gold set.
jgConfusion.how: Cross-tabulation of the judge and human labels.

jgCurve.what: Reliability curve: judge score vs human agreement, per bin.
jgCurve.how: Gold points grouped by judge score.

jgDistribution.what: Distribution of the scores the judge assigned on the gold set.

jgKappaEvo.what: κ evolution over 30 days, compared to the baseline.
jgKappaEvo.how: Kappa per bucket of the judge drift.

jgTopSeg.what: Segments with the most judge-human disagreements.
jgTopSeg.how: Segments sorted by disagreement count, top 4.

jgOverrides.what: Cases where a human overrode the judge's verdict.
jgOverrides.how: Count and share of human overrides on the gold set.

jgRepCases.what: Representative judge-human disagreement cases, with score and status.
jgRepCases.how: Gold points where judge and human diverge.

jgFiche.what: Judge identity: model, number of annotated gold points, release.

jgGates.how: Each threshold compared to its current value gives PASS or watch.

jgRisk.how: Mean of (1−κ, drift/0.10, 1−agreement) × 100; the bullets are attention points.

jgTopDisagree.what: Categories in most disagreement, with their share.

jgSensitive.what: Governed sensitive actions: freeze the judge, change thresholds.
jgSensitive.how: High-impact actions requiring an elevated role or dual control.

security.title: Security & Privacy
security.subtitle: Attacks, PII, least privilege, memory and runtime compliance.

attackRate.what: The share of attacks (prompt injections) that get past the guard.
attackRate.how: Successful attacks ÷ attempted attacks on the adversarial corpus. Lower is better.
attackRate.source: Firewall probe on the adversarial corpus.

blocked.what: The number of prompt injections detected and blocked by the guard.
blocked.how: Count of attempts the firewall refused over the period.

piiLeak.what: The share of answers containing a personal detail that should not have been emitted.
piiLeak.how: Answers with a PII leak ÷ evaluated answers. Target ≤ 0.5%.

leastPriv.what: The gap between tools actually used and those granted to the agent (least privilege).
leastPriv.how: Tools used ÷ tools granted; a wide gap signals superfluous permissions.

sensitiveMemory.what: The number of sensitive memory entries near their expiry (TTL).
sensitiveMemory.how: Entries whose TTL is about to lapse — to purge or renew.

guard.what: The guard's overall efficacy: its F1 (precision/recall balance) against attacks.
guard.how: F1 = harmonic mean of precision/recall; recall = detected ÷ actual attacks.

probes.what: The number of adversarial probes (injections) run against the guard.
probes.how: Count of positive (attack) cases in the fixed adversarial corpus (n_positive).

escaped.what: The number of attacks that slipped past the guard undetected.
escaped.how: False negatives: attacks the firewall failed to block (false_negative).

piiTurns.what: Turns whose response contained personal data, out of all evaluated.

toxicity.what: The share of responses flagged as toxic.

recall.what: The share of real attacks the guard detects.
recall.how: TP / (TP + FN) = detected attacks / real attacks.

precision.what: The share of blocks that hit real attacks (few false positives).
precision.how: TP / (TP + FP) = correct blocks / all blocks.

conformance.what: The share of responses that conform to policy.

overProvCount.what: The number of granted tools never used (excess privilege).
overProvCount.how: Count of granted tools with zero use (n_over_provisioned).

overProvRate.what: The share of granted tools that are excess.

toolMisuse.what: The exposure from over-privilege on the agent's granted tools.
toolMisuse.how: Over-provisioned / granted tools; high = superfluous permissions.

conversations.what: The number of conversations covered by the erasure/evidence surface.
conversations.how: Distinct transcript conversations that have an evidence bundle.

erasure.what: The share of conversations with a complete erasure/evidence bundle.

inversion.what: Memories whose source text can be reconstructed from the embedding (inversion).
inversion.how: n_recoverable / n_memories above the similarity threshold.

isolationProbes.what: The number of cross-tenant isolation checks run.
isolationProbes.how: Count of turns tested for cross-tenant leakage.

isolationLeaks.what: The number of turns that leaked another tenant's data.
isolationLeaks.how: Count of turns where isolation failed.

domainCases.what: The non-regression harness cases failing for this domain.
domainCases.how: Cases where the agent fails, filtered by domain category.

redteam.what: Blocked injections vs bypasses from the adversarial campaign.
redteam.how: True positives blocked / total, with the bypasses (false negatives).

trend.what: The 30-day risk trend from the durable scores.
trend.how: 1 - faithfulness mean (attacks) and 1 - grounding mean (incidents) per bucket.

refusal.what: The balance between over- and under-refusal of the guard.
refusal.how: Over-refusal rate (legit refused) and under-refusal (forbidden allowed).

overPriv.what: The per-tool granted-vs-used detail, flagging the excess.
overPriv.how: Tools in the granted set with low or no use.

isolationFacts.what: How tenant isolation is enforced (a fact, not a metric).
isolationFacts.how: Separation by environment, schema and session state.

failures.how: Count per family: injection, tool misuse, inversion, refusal, PII, toxicity.

regression.what: The probability that the guard regresses.

domainRisk.what: The normalized risk per security domain.
domainRisk.how: Max of the domain's real rates (injection, privacy, tools, memory, compliance).

priorityCases.what: The most severe failed cases to handle first.
priorityCases.how: First harness cases sorted by severity.

zoneActual.what: The live snapshot of the security posture.
zoneActual.how: Current values of each headline security signal.

zoneControls.what: The load-bearing security controls, with their target threshold.
zoneControls.how: Each control's live value vs its target + owner + case.

zoneDiagnostic.what: The root-cause diagnostics behind the posture.
zoneDiagnostic.how: Failure distribution, refusal calibration, recent changes, priority cases.

zonePredictive.how: Risk trend, regression probability, per-domain risk, over-privilege.

zonePrivacy.how: Red-team blocks, erasure completeness, memory inversion.

zoneActions.what: The governed remediations for the current posture.
zoneActions.how: Each card leads to a dual-control action (freeze, playbook, purge).

railIncidents.what: The most severe open security cases.
railIncidents.how: Top failed harness cases, sorted by severity.

railGates.how: PASS/WATCH/FAIL from the precision and conformance thresholds.

railSiem.how: Real case ids + severities (+ anomaly count).

crossTenant.what: The share of turns that leaked another tenant's data.
crossTenant.how: n_leaks / n_turns of the cross-tenant isolation test. Target 0%.

panel.trendNote: proxy: hallucination failure rate over the window

act.redteamDesc: Enrich the attack set and replay.

rail.notWired: Not wired — governed purge is coming in a dedicated lot

tabx.isolationFactSchema: Dedicated Postgres schema per environment: transcript, scores, ledger and corpus are isolated via search_path.

tabx.noCases: No failed cases in this domain.

compliance.title: Compliance
compliance.subtitle: Regulatory posture derived from real runtime signals.

score.what: The agent's overall compliance level, derived continuously from runtime signals.
score.how: Weighted aggregation of conformant / partial / non-conformant controls across the tracked frameworks.
score.source: Runtime signals mapped to frameworks (DORA, GDPR, AI Act…).

obligations.what: The number of regulatory obligations covered by at least one control.
obligations.how: Obligations with a mapped control, out of all tracked frameworks.

conformant.what: The number of controls whose runtime evidence satisfies the obligation.

partial.what: Partially satisfied controls — incomplete evidence or near the threshold.

nonConformant.what: Failing controls: the obligation is not satisfied.

residual.what: Risks remaining despite the controls in place, under watch.
residual.how: Identified, unclosed risks, weighted by severity.

deadlines.what: The near regulatory deadlines that require action.
deadlines.how: Obligations or remediations whose due date is approaching.

mapping.what: Compliance score per regulatory framework (DORA, GDPR, BaFin, CNIL…).
mapping.how: One framework per row; score = share of conformant controls.

obligTable.what: Applicable regulatory obligations: status, deadline, owner.
obligTable.how: One row per obligation; status applied or in progress.

evidence.what: Completeness of audit evidence: valid, missing, blocking.
evidence.how: Share of valid evidence over the expected total.

controls.how: One row per control: conformant, partial or non-conformant.

missing.what: Controls with no valid evidence, with the framework concerned.
missing.how: Non-conformant controls mapped to their expected evidence.

incidents.what: Open non-conformities: severity and handling status.

businessLegal.what: Business signals whose manifest declares a legal engagement.
businessLegal.how: Selective projection of AgentSpec business_signals with engagement=legal; the value comes from real business scores.

rail.lastEvalMissing: Not captured — the report does not carry an evaluation date yet
rail.notWired: Not wired — no processing registry exists yet

reliability.title: Reliability & cost
reliability.subtitle: Availability, latency, errors and the agent's economic cost.

availability.what: The share of time the service answered correctly (operational availability).
availability.how: 1 − (errored requests ÷ total requests) over the window.

errorRate.what: The share of requests that ended in error (tool denied, failure, timeout…).
errorRate.how: Errored ÷ total requests over the window. Lower is better.

p50.what: Median latency: half of requests answer faster.
p50.how: 50th percentile of end-to-end response time over the window.

p95.what: Tail latency: 95% of requests answer below this — reveals spikes.

toolSuccess.what: The share of tool calls that succeed (no denial or argument error).

totalCost.what: Total LLM cost over the window: tokens consumed × model rate.
totalCost.how: Sum of tokens per request × rate per model.

costPerReq.how: Total cost ÷ number of requests over the window.

requests.what: The volume of requests handled over the window.

latency.what: Response latency by percentile: p50 / p95 / p99 = the duration below which 50%, 95%, and 99% of turns fall, respectively.
latency.how: Percentiles computed over observed turn durations in the period.

availErrors.what: Availability and error rate overlaid over time.
availErrors.how: Two series per interval: availability (1 minus errors) and error rate.

errors.how: Count of errors grouped by type over the window.

costPerDay.how: Sum of estimated costs per day.

volumePerDay.what: Number of requests handled per day.

costByModel.what: Cost, requests, pass-rate and latency per model.
costByModel.how: One row per model over the window.

servicesCost.what: Most costly services, with requests, cost and share.
servicesCost.how: Services sorted by cost; share = cost / total.

incidents.what: Recent reliability incidents: date, type, service, severity.
incidents.how: Events from the incident register over the window.

actions.what: Prioritised corrective actions: priority, impact, complexity.
actions.how: Actions derived from reliability and cost signals.

services.what: Success rate, p50 latency and requests per service.

providers.what: Share of requests per LLM provider.
providers.how: Requests per provider relative to the total.

budget.what: Monthly budget: spent, projected, and within or over budget.
budget.how: Cumulative spent, linear monthly projection, against the threshold.

qualityTrend.what: Recent quality score and its trend.
qualityTrend.how: Last point of the quality series and its delta.

panel.availNote: Current availability & error rate (no per-day breakdown)

rail.qualityTrendNote: Mean quality score of judged answers

improvement.title: Improvement
improvement.subtitle: Prioritise, run and measure quality remediations for your AI agents.

gain.what: The quality gain achievable if the priority improvements are applied.
gain.how: Sum of the estimated gains (in points) of the open opportunities.

actions.what: The number of active improvement actions recommended by the analysis.
actions.how: Opportunities in an active status (to start / in progress).

curate.what: The number of cases awaiting curation to enrich the eval set.
curate.how: Flagged cases (low score, failure) not yet curated.

frozen.what: The number of frozen deployments (quality gate not passed).
frozen.how: Releases blocked by a guard or an exhausted error budget.

shadow.what: Candidates to test in shadow traffic or by replay before production.
shadow.how: Variants ready to compare without impacting users.

coverage.what: The agent's evaluation coverage, with corpus debt (age) and the number of cases to curate.
coverage.how: Coverage = share of cases covered by the eval set; debt = age of the oldest corpus item (days); to-curate = pending cases.

debt.what: The corpus's age: how long since it was last refreshed.
debt.how: Days since the last significant ingestion or update.

roi.what: The estimated return on investment of the improvements versus their cost.
roi.how: Expected gain relative to estimated effort.

opportunities.what: Prioritised improvement actions: cause, estimated gain, effort, risk, owner.
opportunities.how: One row per opportunity, sorted by gain.
opportunities.source: Improvement analysis (derived from failed cases and quality signals).

causes.what: Breakdown of the root causes of quality problems.

candidate.what: Deployment-candidate version and the state of its quality gates.
candidate.how: Each gate compared to its threshold gives PASS or watch.

topProblems.what: Addressable problems with the highest gain delivered.

current.how: Current version read from the report.

sensitive.what: Governed shortcuts to high-impact actions (freeze, prompts, corpus).
sensitive.how: Links to governed pages; elevated role required.

cta.curationDesc: Curate failing cases and cover the missing intents.
cta.experimentsDesc: Replay the candidates in shadow before any production rollout.
cta.releaseDesc: Check the quality / coverage / corpus gates, then publish.
cta.experimentsNote: Shadow-traffic / replay candidates are the datasets whose drift exceeds the threshold: replay them in shadow before publishing.

open.what: The number of incidents currently open (unresolved).
open.how: Incidents in open or in-progress status over the window.

critical.what: The number of critical-severity incidents still in progress.

mtta.what: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): from trigger to acknowledgement, averaged over 7 days.
mtta.how: Mean (acknowledged − triggered) over the last 7 days' incidents.

mttr.what: Mean time to resolve (MTTR): from trigger to closure, averaged over 7 days.
mttr.how: Mean (closed − triggered) over the last 7 days' incidents.

playbooks.what: The number of incident procedures (playbooks) currently running.

autoresolve.what: The share of incidents resolved automatically, with no human intervention.
autoresolve.how: Auto-resolved incidents ÷ total incidents over the period.

evidence.what: The number of evidence packs generated from incidents.
evidence.how: Evidence packs produced over the window.

sla_risk.what: The number of incidents at risk of breaching their service deadline (SLA).
sla_risk.how: Incidents whose time remaining before the SLA deadline is low.

queue.what: The incident triage queue, ordered by priority (severity crossed with SLA deadline).
queue.how: Open incidents sorted by severity then remaining SLA time.

sla.what: SLA escalations: incidents whose service deadline is approaching, with time remaining.
sla.how: Time remaining before SLA breach, per incident.

incidents.title: Incidents & playbooks
incidents.subtitle: Incident response, playbook orchestration and governed remediation.

durable.title: Declared incidents
durable.empty: No declared incident — open the first one via “Create incident”.

cassette.title: Execution cassettes
cassette.empty: No cassette captured — every grounded turn is captured automatically as soon as a customer talks to the agent.
cassette.pick: Select a cassette to read its recorded execution: trace, assembled prompt, parameters, tool calls — then replay it against a candidate model.
cassette.notFound: Cassette “{id}” is no longer within the 100 most recent captures.
cassette.question: Question (masked)
cassette.traceEmpty: No execution shape was captured for this cassette.
cassette.traceUnpositioned: Capture predates real offsets — durations only, no position and no total (parallel nodes overlap).
cassette.orphanTools: Tool calls with no attributed node
cassette.promptNotCaptured: Prompt not captured — cassette predates the S2 capture, or the turn had no LLM synthesis.
cassette.replayFrozen: As-of reading — one does not act in the past.
cassette.replayFailed: Replay failed (model unavailable or cassette evicted).

cassettes.what: Every grounded turn is captured as a replayable cassette: masked question, retrieved context, answer, assembled prompt, sampling, tool calls and real node offsets.
cassettes.how: Selection lives in the URL (?bundle=), shareable. Replay regenerates the answer on the same (question, context) pair with the candidate model, re-judges it and shows the score delta. Whatever was not captured reads “not captured”, never invented.
cassettes.source: Append-only bundles.jsonl store (S2 capture, rails registry XT-01)

actual.what: The current state of replay / shadow traffic: volumes, deviations and coverage over the period.
actual.how: Summary of replay KPIs aggregated over the observation window.

diagnostic.what: Where divergences between replay and the baseline come from, broken down by type, severity and sessions.
diagnostic.how: Deviations classified by type and severity over replayed traffic.

comparisons.what: Detailed comparisons: top deviations, recent comparisons and regressions vs the baseline.
comparisons.how: Compares each replay to its baseline and ranks divergences.

distribution.what: The distribution of replayed traffic (by service, by model) and the associated proofs/exports.
distribution.how: Breakdown of replayed requests and proof status.

sessions.what: The number of captured sessions that went through the replay engine.
sessions.how: Count of recent captured bundles (capped at the last 100), not the number of actual replays.

requests.what: The number of logged replayed requests.
requests.how: Size of the replay journal (capped at 500), cumulative — not an N-day window.

tokens.what: The replayed tokens — not available in this build.
tokens.how: Bundles carry no token counter; the value stays a dash.

cost.what: The replay cost — not available in this build.
cost.how: Without a token counter no cost can be computed; the value stays a dash.

deviations.what: The number of critical deviations vs the reference.
deviations.how: Replays whose score drops by 0.10+ vs baseline, PLUS eval cases passing at run N-1 and failing at run N.

evals.what: The number of eval runs compared (offline, model llama3.2:3b).
evals.how: Sum of per-agent pass-rate records from the eval reports — not shadow-traffic replays.

proofs.what: The generated proofs — not available in this build.
proofs.how: Replay proof subsystem not implemented; the value stays a dash.

coverage.how: No eligible-traffic denominator is computed; the value stays a dash.

devByType.what: The breakdown of deviations by type (content, format, tool, refusal…) versus the baseline.

severity.what: The breakdown of deviations by severity (critical → low).

byService.what: The breakdown of replayed traffic by calling service.

byModel.what: The breakdown of replayed traffic by model.

regressions.what: The services whose quality regresses the most versus the baseline.
regressions.how: Top services by negative score gap vs baseline.

traffic.how: Bars = captured bundles per day (last 100); the tokens line stays at zero (bundles have no tokens).

recentSessions.how: The 6 latest bundles; status replayed if the bundle has already been executed via replay, else done.

baselines.how: Each agent's latest real eval run (with its catalogue).

topDeviations.what: The 10 largest deviations vs the reference.
topDeviations.how: A mix of two sources: replays with a large score delta (numeric Δ) and eval cases passed then failed (passed then failed).

comparisons.what: The recent run comparisons per agent.
comparisons.how: An agent with at least 2 eval runs: current vs previous run; sessions = eval-case count, deviations = newly failed cases.

evalsByCat.how: Note: identical to the deviations-by-type distribution — a count of newly failed cases per category, not replays.

proofsExports.how: Demonstration: all values stay dashes, with no real source.

activity.how: Stream of the latest replay events (id, time, status).

replay.title: Replay & shadow
replay.subtitle: Replay sessions precisely, compare against baselines and observe shadow traffic.

rail.shadowNote: Replays the latest captured turns against a candidate model (2 turns, real judge).

footer.source: Source of truth: Replay log · bundles.jsonl

tabx.shadowExplain: Shadow traffic (fleet mirroring onto a candidate model) is not implemented in this build: nothing is displayed rather than invented figures. REAL replays are launched from the Console and feed the replay journal.

actual.what: The current curation state: candidates, promotable, to-review and rejected over the period.
actual.how: Summary of curation KPIs aggregated over the observation window.

diagnostic.what: Why cases enter curation: priority lots and the reasons retained tours were kept.
diagnostic.how: Lots scored by risk + most frequent inclusion reasons.

gaps.what: Eval-set coverage gaps (by intent, by language) and the candidate distribution.

governance.what: Governed curation actions (freeze, create replay, export) and recent activity.
governance.how: Available lot actions + recent operations log.

trends.what: Trends: curation backlog, set balance and the impact of curation on quality.

sections.heading: What is Tessera?
body: Tessera is a control tower for a bank's AI agents. Picture a bank that employs several AI assistants: one answers customer questions, another guides new customers through opening an account, a third handles overdue payments. They were built by different teams, sometimes on different technologies. Yet someone must be able to answer three simple questions: what are these agents doing? Are they doing it well? And can you prove it, evidence in hand, to an auditor?
Tessera is where those three questions get their answers.

The bank you are visiting, Crédit Aurore, is fictional — this is a demonstration. Everything else works for real: the agents genuinely answer, the numbers are genuinely measured, and Tessera builds a tamper-proof evidence ledger. Every head is sealed by a qualified RFC 3161 timestamp that can be verified outside Tessera; the screen grants that status only after a successful cryptographic check. Whenever something is simulated, the screen tells you so. It is a house rule; you will see it everywhere.

sections.heading: The bank and the cockpit
body: From the very first page, Tessera asks you to pick a space: the bank, or the cockpit that supervises it. That separation is not an interface detail: it is the heart of the system.

The business spaces are the bank as its customers and advisors live it: the Crédit Aurore website with its assistant, the advisor's console for overdue payments. Nothing there betrays the machinery — deliberately. A customer should never see backstage.
The cockpit is the engine room: the fleet of agents, their signals, their trust levels, their evidence. This is where the operator works — the person accountable for the fleet.
Between the two there is a single door, one way only: the operator may go see what customers experience; the reverse is impossible.

sections.heading: How Tessera observes agents
body: Every agent continuously publishes the story of its activity: how many conversations, which decisions, what outcomes. Tessera never reaches inside an agent — the agent publishes, the cockpit reads. Much like a Holter monitor: the sensor records the heart living its life, without ever touching it.

What makes the idea powerful is that it does not depend on who built the agent. Any agent can be observed — another team's, another vendor's, another technology — as long as it publishes in the expected language. You have living proof in the fleet: Hello Agent was written without a single line of this project, and its level badge is computed from real measurements anyway. We timed its full onboarding: twenty minutes and eighteen seconds.

sections.heading: How Tessera tests agents
body: Observing is not always enough. Is an agent that has been silent for two hours healthy, or down? As long as nobody talks to it, there is no way to know. You need to be able to prompt it.

That is the second contract: an agent may declare a test door. The operator uses it to send a trial message from the cockpit — before entrusting the agent to real customers, or to reproduce a problem a customer reported. And an automatic mechanism, the canary, sends a trial message at regular intervals, so that silence never means "we don't know".
If observation is the Holter monitor, testing is the stress test: you make the heart work under controlled conditions, precisely because waiting is not enough.

Three safeguards accompany every trial, without exception. It is authenticated: we know who sent it. It is recorded: it leaves a trace in the audit ledger. And it is marked as synthetic: a test message will never be counted as a real customer in the bank's numbers.
In production, Tessera watches everything, touches almost nothing, and forgets nothing.

sections.heading: Why some agents serve no clients
body: Three agents in the fleet may intrigue you: they carry a "Platform witness" chip and serve nobody. Hello Agent, Turn Agent and Duplex Agent are witnesses: each proves one capability of the platform, and only one.

Hello Agent proves you can observe a foreign agent: it publishes its activity but cannot be tested. Turn Agent proves the reverse: you can test it from the cockpit, but it publishes nothing. Duplex Agent proves the two combine: you prompt it, it acts, its activity shows up, and its trust level rises because it was tested. The full loop.

Why keep them so bare? Because their simplicity is the proof. If the observable witness needed to be testable in order to work, the demonstration would prove nothing anymore. Each one shows that a capability stands on its own — and Duplex shows they assemble.

sections.heading: What is real, and what is merely declared
body: Tessera follows a simple rule: a number on screen is a number that was measured. When a piece of data does not exist yet, the screen shows a dash and tells you why — never a fake zero, never an invented score.

You will see it on the fleet's badges. "L1 computed" means: this level rests on real measurements. "L2 declared · no evidence" means: the agent announces capabilities the platform has not yet been able to verify. The difference is displayed, not hidden.
Most dashboards show you their best profile. This one tells you where every number comes from — which is rarer, and makes all the difference the day an auditor asks.

sections.heading: The two memories
body: Tessera keeps two memories, and telling them apart illuminates everything else.
The first records what the agents do: conversations, measurements, business events. That is the raw material of the dashboards.

The second records what we decide about them: this reply was validated by an advisor, this message was blocked by a rule, this agent was tested by the operator on Tuesday at 2:07 pm. That is the audit ledger. Each entry is chained to the previous one, like links in a chain: none can be altered or removed without it showing. This is what you hand to an auditor.
One sentence keeps them apart: the first memory tells what the agents do; the second, what humans decide about them.

proof.text: the Prove page, and the integrity badge at the bottom of every screen.

sections.heading: Going further
body: Every architecture decision in Tessera is written down, dated and argued in a decision log — including the mistakes and their corrections, because a system that documents only its successes documents nothing. Two stories cover the most instructive moments: the day the audit ledger forked, and the twenty minutes it took to onboard a foreign agent. If you are in the field, start there.
